audit_baseline: Supplied UI4ME Core v0.2 capability register; 125 rows; original text retained unchanged in audit_* fields.
qualification_policy: Implementation, runtime availability and platform qualification are different states. This scope ledger does not assert current-candidate native qualification. Windows R05 remains open until independent UIA text-selection/read verification succeeds.
delivery_sequence: Complete implementation in the candidate repository.
Qualify Python applications on native KDE Wayland first; debug, commit and push only after that gate passes.
Qualify the same source on Windows Server 2022 under a normal RDP user; debug, commit and push only after that gate passes.
Run final regression/stabilization on both target environments.
scope_policy: All 125 rows have a disposition. Excluded rows do not imply a promised later version. Reusable components and virtualization belong above Core. Native Wayland and Windows are the implementation targets; no X11 or macOS qualification is asserted.

capabilities.name: Distinguish implemented support, current availability, and qualified behavior
capabilities.audit_owner: Native host protocol and platform qualification; cross-cutting audit reporting
capabilities.audit_baseline_behavior: host.capabilities mostly derives clipboard, dialogs, external-open, DnD, IME, and accessibility flags from !headless. It already reports tray=false, printing=false, Windows-only positioning, and native_qualification='requires local evidence'. These flags do not probe portal availability, compositor extensions, assistive-technology activation, or RDP behavior. Linux dependency features enable Wayland only; native dialogs explicitly require a Wayland handle.
capabilities.audit_existing_primitive: Existing structured capabilities/errors, optional winit extension queries, portal interface/version discovery, and backend-specific return values are enough; no new capability library is needed.
capabilities.audit_completion_guidance: Stabilize the meaning of current flags as implemented support if that is their intent, and keep actual operation errors truthful. Where applications need adaptation, add separate observed/unknown availability fields or narrow operation capabilities. Do not advertise topmost, global shortcuts, X11, or native preference tracking merely because a dependency contains an API. Runtime probing is optional unless the public field promises runtime availability.
capabilities.candidate_behavior: host.capabilities schema 2 separates implemented support, observed/unknown availability and qualification/scope. Headless or missing-service states do not automatically become successful native support.
capabilities.limits: Native qualification is evidence-driven. No new build is automatically declared qualified by a feature flag or dependency API.

capabilities.name: Parent-aware external open and reveal-in-file-manager
capabilities.audit_baseline_behavior: desktop.open_external already opens approved URI/path targets through Linux OpenURI/OpenFile/OpenDirectory or Windows ShellExecuteW. capabilities.audit_completion_guidance: Optionally accept a window owner, retain/export it for the handoff, and preserve asynchronous error semantics. capabilities.candidate_behavior: External-open accepts an optional originating window and uses the parent-capable OpenURI/Win32 path; chooser operations retain cancellation. Reveal uses FileManager1.ShowItems or SHOpenFolderAndSelectItems.

capabilities.name: Element-level incoming drop policy and drag feedback

The host accepts Copy for text or URI offers at window level, tracks the pointer, and emits the completed drop to the hit element. capabilities.audit_completion_guidance: Register accepted drop types/actions before the gesture, compute element acceptance synchronously in the host, expose bounded hover feedback, and reconcile completion with document replacement and cancellation. Keep current text/file Copy behavior stable; richer drop negotiation is an additive feature rather than a prerequisite for using existing drops.
capabilities.candidate_behavior: Element-level incoming file/text drop policy uses data-ui4me-drop, gives Copy/reject feedback, and retains/revalidates the original document and node after asynchronous transfers.
capabilities.limits: Transfers are bounded to 1MiB text / 1024 paths. This does not enable outgoing native drags or general DataTransfer browser semantics.
capabilities.qualification: Current candidate requires cloud checks and sequential Linux KDE/Python then Windows Server 2022/RDP qualification; no native pass is asserted here.

capabilities.audit_baseline_behavior: Declarative shadow roots are explicitly refused and remain inert template contents; style adapters return no shadow root. Custom-named tags can be ordinary styled elements, but there is no registry, lifecycle or encapsulated component tree.
capabilities.audit_existing_primitive: HTML parsing and normal DOM/CSS composition; template primitives can support UI-library components without browser lifecycle machinery.
capabilities.audit_completion_guidance: Full support would require shadow trees, slotting, scoped cascade, composed event/focus/a11y traversal and an explicit component runtime. Keep application component composition above Core unless a concrete web-component compatibility requirement justifies that expansion.
capabilities.candidate_behavior: Do not expose or implement this additional feature in the frozen Core 1.0 batch. The audit baseline description below records any underlying primitive or existing behavior; dependency support is not a public Core promise.
capabilities.limits: No scheduled later release is implied. Revisit only if an actual application requirement justifies changing the frozen scope.
capabilities.qualification: Excluded extension; no implementation or native qualification is claimed.

capabilities.name: Native application and context menus
capabilities.audit_owner: UI library by default; optional native-host extension when explicitly required
capabilities.audit_baseline_behavior: There is no native menu model, command routing, accelerator registration, or platform menu lifecycle in the public host contract. Document-rendered menus can instead be built using the UI library and existing events.
capabilities.audit_existing_primitive: muda provides native menus, but its Linux implementation uses GTK rather than dropping into the current winit Wayland stack. Windows menu accelerators also require message-loop integration. A menu library does not supply UI4ME's command/lifecycle contract.
capabilities.audit_completion_guidance: Keep ordinary menus in the UI library. If native menus become a concrete requirement, design stable menu/item IDs, state updates, command routing, keyboard behavior, popup ownership, and platform adapters; assess GTK/runtime implications before adoption.

capabilities.name: Contenteditable and rich HTML clipboard
capabilities.audit_owner: Optional editor package; host MIME support if authorized
capabilities.audit_baseline_behavior: Substantial inherited editing and rich clipboard code remains. Hosted documents reject active contenteditable including plaintext-only, and rich clipboard commands are excluded.
capabilities.audit_existing_primitive: Donor editor, formatting/history, sanitizer and HTML clipboard model.
capabilities.audit_completion_guidance: A supported editor needs async rich MIME on both OSes and consistent IME, selection, undo, layout, accessibility and malformed-input behavior; removing the gate is insufficient.

capabilities.name: SMIL and SVG document animation
capabilities.audit_baseline_behavior: Animation elements are stripped/reported, and usvg/resvg is a static SVG engine. Ordinary CSS animations elsewhere already exist.
capabilities.audit_existing_primitive: Application-driven DOM updates and whole-image CSS transforms cover many UI effects.
capabilities.audit_completion_guidance: Keep SMIL outside the Core baseline. A full animation timing/interpolation system would be a separate undertaking; use existing application/CSS animation for actual needs.
